smm_pool.title: 20 Social Media Metrics to Track (With Formulas and Benchmarks)
smm_pool.text: More doesn't necessarily mean better . Think emails in your inbox, glitter on a Mother's Day card, hot sauce… That applies to social media metrics, too. It's tempting to track everything your analytics dashboard throws at you. But not all social media metrics are created equal, and the ones worth your time come down to your specific social media marketing goals — whether that's testing a new format, growing an audience, or getting more people to your website. Metrics are most helpful when they guide your next move — adjusting your content, switching up your posting schedule, or even thinking up new products. In this guide, I'll walk you through 20 social media marketing metrics, what each one tells you, how to calculate it, and how to turn the right handful into KPIs. Key takeaways Social media metrics vs. KPIs: Metrics are everything you can measure on your accounts. KPIs are the three to five metrics you tie to a specific goal and target, such as lifting LinkedIn engagement rate from 4% to 6% in a quarter. Engagement rate is the most widely used metric for judging whether content is landing. The formula is total engagements ÷ reach × 100. Typical engagement rates differ by platform. Buffer’s analysis of 52+ million posts found 2025 medians of about 6.2% on LinkedIn, 5.6% on Facebook, 5.5% on Instagram, 4.6% on TikTok, 4.0% on Pinterest, 3.6% on Threads, and 2.5% on X. Reach vs. impressions: Reach counts the unique people who saw a post. Impressions, which many platforms now report as views, count every time it was shown, including repeats. Replying to comments is linked to higher engagement on every platform Buffer studied, with up to 42% more on Threads and 30% more on LinkedIn. Posting consistently protects your growth. In Buffer’s data, accounts that skipped a week of posting grew followers more slowly than their own usual rate. Vanity metrics like follower count and likes are most useful when you turn them into a rate, such as follower growth rate or engagement rate. Click-through rate, conversion rate, and return on ad spend are the metrics that connect social media activity to revenue. smm_pool.title: How to Schedule a Post on Facebook — for Pages, Profiles + Groups
smm_pool.text: I run a Facebook group called Freelancers Who Work Smart, Not Hard , but, for ages, I managed it the hard way, not the smart way. The hard way looks like this: trying to remember to post regularly (when I sometimes can’t even remember what day of the week it is), coming up with some of my best ideas at 3 a.m. (before promptly falling asleep and forgetting them), and posting sporadically with neither consistency nor strategy. Days or even weeks (eek) would go by without me posting, and the group would lose momentum. Somewhat ironically, things changed when I went on maternity leave. Before taking three months off work, I scheduled two posts a week to keep the group active while I was dealing with diapers. In doing so, the group became more active than it’s ever been! So in the interest of working smarter, not harder — whether you run a Facebook Page, a profile in professional mode, or a Facebook Group — let me walk you through how to set up a similar process. The short version: you can schedule a post on Facebook natively from a Page, a professional-mode profile, or a Group you admin, but not from a regular personal profile. In this guide, I'll walk you through how to schedule a post on Facebook three ways: in the Facebook app, in Meta Business Suite, and with Buffer. I'll also cover what to do when the schedule option goes missing, and how to find, edit, or delete posts you've already scheduled. Key takeaways You can schedule a post on Facebook natively from a Facebook Page, a profile in professional mode, or a Facebook Group you admin or moderate. Regular personal profiles can't schedule posts. Meta Business Suite schedules posts to Facebook Pages and Instagram, but not to Facebook Groups. Buffer publishes scheduled Facebook Page posts automatically and sends Facebook Group posts to your phone as a notification to publish yourself. It doesn't connect to personal or professional-mode profiles. If the option to schedule is missing, the most common causes are posting from a regular personal profile or not having admin access to the Page or Group. You can edit, reschedule, or delete a scheduled post on Facebook, Meta Business Suite, or, for posts you scheduled there, in Buffer's calendar. Buffer's analysis of more than 1 million Facebook posts found that posts shared at 9 a.m. on Thursday performed best. Jump to a section: Can you schedule a post on Facebook?
